[independent-corroboration from #2214] Defect (2) — the worktree/main interpreter divergence — independently re-derived during #2214's implementation round, with a FLEET-WIDE measurement this body did not have. #2417 measured one worktree (issue-2329-q35-ladder-decay at 3.12.13 vs main at 3.11.15); the split is much wider than that.

**All 25 live worktrees, interpreter read directly from each `.venv/bin/python` (2026-08-20 ~15:5xZ): 19 at 3.12.13, 6 at 3.11.15, root at 3.11.15.**

- 3.11.15 (6): issue-779, issue-1336-backward, issue-1336-fullcorpora, issue-1739, issue-2058, issue-2061 — all older worktrees.
- 3.12.13 (19): i1739-fit, issue-2201, issue-2205, issue-2212, issue-2214, issue-2217, issue-2228, issue-2329-q35-ladder-decay, issue-2356, issue-2378, issue-2379, issue-2388, issue-2389, issue-2412, issue-2422, issue-2428, issue-823-ladder, mc-flip, mc-rung0-fix1 — i.e. every RECENTLY created worktree.

So the divergence is not a one-off on #2329's tree: it is the DEFAULT for new worktrees, and the Step 9c gate is currently certifying diffs on a non-canonical interpreter for roughly three quarters of live worktrees.

**Mechanism, confirmed:** no `.python-version` exists at the root or in any worktree, and none is tracked (`git ls-files | grep -c '^\.python-version$'` returns 0). `scripts/new_worktree.sh` never creates or pins a venv (`grep -nE "venv|python-version|uv sync|uv venv" scripts/new_worktree.sh` → no matches), so each worktree's first incidental `uv run` materializes a venv at whatever `uv` prefers for `requires-python = ">=3.11"` — currently 3.12.13 — while the long-lived root venv is 3.11.15 and `ruff target-version = "py311"`. The interpreter a worktree gets is therefore a function of WHEN it was created, not of any recorded decision.

**Second independent sighting of the same `test_issue2329_r2_fixes.py::test_atomic_writers…` red**, reached without knowledge of this task: #2214's implementer ran its post-change full suite in the 3.12.13 worktree, saw that failure absent from the 3.11.15 root baseline, and attributed it to the 3.11→3.12 lambda-pickle message change by reverting its own diff and re-running in the same venv (red both ways ⇒ pre-existing, not a #2214 regression). That is exactly the "teaches sessions to discount test failures" cost this body names — and it also cost a real detour: the confound forced per-test attribution to reach a trustworthy regression verdict, because a worktree-vs-root suite comparison is confounded by default while this is open.

**Notes toward defect (2)'s disposition**, offered as input rather than a decision:

- The canonical-interpreter choice looks like a genuine project call, not a mechanical one: 3.11.15 matches the root venv and `ruff target-version = py311`; 3.12.13 matches 19 of 25 live worktrees. Pinning whichever one the fleet is NOT converging on will keep re-creating drift.
- Prefer a WARN-on-mismatch probe plus rebuild-on-next-create over a fleet-wide forced rebuild — 19 divergent worktrees include many with live sessions mid-round, and rebuilding a venv under a running session is its own incident. `new_worktree.sh` already has the right idiom for this in its once-per-session `/mnt/eps-data` bind WARN.
- A pin test (a tracked `.python-version` exists AND agrees with `requires-python` / `target-version`) is what stops the pin from silently rotting back to this state.

**Duplicate housekeeping:** I filed #2429 for defect (2) before seeing this task — #2417 predates it by ~10 hours and covers strictly more (this body has both defects; mine had only the interpreter half). #2429 is archived as a duplicate pointing here; no action needed on it. #2214 itself is unaffected: its fix is interpreter-independent and was verified green on BOTH 3.12.13 and 3.11.15.
